subject: Escape pathway incentive package for Brightline — pricing & migration credit proposal
messages:
From: Alexa Ruiz <alexa@brightline.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing parity ask + migration credit (Brightline)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. We ran an internal evaluation and are lining up a migration from our current OpenAI/Cloud endpoints, but pricing is the primary gating factor for our execs. A few data points to help frame the ask:

- Current monthly average spend (production): ~$180k/month.
- Peak Q4 forecast: ~$350k/mo if we convert a new product line.
- Current blended per-token effective price (post-commercial discounts): ~ $0.00075 / prompt-token, $0.00175 / completion-token (we have a mix of chat + few-shot generation).
- We're evaluating a 12–18 month committed plan if unit economics align.

Two concrete asks:
1) Can Redwood match or come within 10% of our effective blended unit cost vs our current vendor?
2) Can you include a migration incentive (one-time credit or upfront rebate) to offset termination/engineering costs?

Attached is a light RFP export of our usage buckets and sample prompts for sizing (Brightline_RFP.csv). Procurement is looped at procurement@brightline.ai for contracting.

High level timeline: procurement wants a commercial term sheet by next Monday (Nov 9) to present to their CFO. Would appreciate a written proposal with an indicative committed tier and any conditions.

—Alexa
Alexa Ruiz
Director of Platform — Brightline.ai

[Attachment: Brightline_RFP.csv (CSV)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alexa Ruiz <alexa@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing parity ask + migration credit (Brightline)

Hi Alexa —

Thanks for the data and timeline. We can put together a displacement package that targets parity with your effective blended unit price. To make the proposal tight for procurement I need two small clarifications:

- Can you confirm the current split (approx) between prompt vs completion tokens (prompt % vs completion %)?
- Do you need invoice-level monthly metering or consolidated quarterly billing for your finance team?

High-level note: we have three levers that drive unit economics for a migration: committed monthly minimum, multi-month term, and an onboarding migration credit. We can combine those into an "Escape Pathway" (one-off credit + short-term committed discount) to make switching cash-flow neutral.

I'll draft a commercial sheet with a few options and loop in our pricing lead Ben for approval on the credit quantum. Can you confirm whether DocuSign is acceptable for contract signature? If so we'll include a prepared term sheet link.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Key constraints from customer: ~180k/mo today, peaks 350k/mo; willing to commit 12–18 months if economics align.

Can you suggest 2–3 compact commercial options we can present:
- Option A: low-commit (month-to-month) with small migration credit
- Option B: 12-month commit with unit price parity and higher credit
- Option C: 18-month commit + marketplace/implementation credits + SLA uplift

Ben replied: 
> Karthik — see rough constructs below. All numbers indicative, will need legal to check clauses on credits.
> 
> Option A (Light trial): No commit, standard hosted rates, migration credit = $30k one-time (applied as invoice credit over first 3 months). Great for low friction PoC.
> 
> Option B (12-month commit): Commit $1.8M over 12 months (avg $150k/mo). Unit pricing target: $0.00068 / prompt-token, $0.0016 / completion-token (these are ~9% below their current blended). Migration credit = $85k (applied up-front as invoice credit month 1). 30-day termination with repayment schedule on unused credit. Includes 4 hours onboarding R&D + 1 performance tuning pass.
> 
> Option C (18-month aggressive): Commit $3.0M over 18 months (avg $166k/mo). Unit pricing: $0.00060 / prompt-token, $0.00145 / completion-token (~15% improvement). Migration credit = $150k (split $75k upfront, $75k after first 3 months if usage thresholds met). Includes 8 hours professional services, elevated SLA (99.9% for inference), and optional marketplace credits for cloud escape.

> 
> Ben

Marissa — any implementation caveats we should call out (networking, private VPC needs) in the cover note?

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial proposal — Escape Pathway options for Brightline (deck attached)

Hi Alexa / Brightline procurement —

Appreciate the context and timeline. Attached is an indicative commercial sheet and term summary (Redwood_Brightline_Commercial_Sheet_v1.pdf) with three succinct options to support migration off your current provider. High level summary below — this is intended to be negotiation-ready for your Nov 9 procurement review: 

Option A — Low-friction PoC (fast start)- Commit: None (hosted pay-as-you-go)- Pricing: standard hosted rates (no guaranteed parity)- Migration credit: $30,000 one-time, applied as invoice credit across first 3 invoices- Key fit: low risk, fast cutover, limited financial upside

Option B — 12-month Escape (recommended middle ground)- Commit: $1.8M over 12 months (avg $150k/mo)- Unit pricing (indicative): $0.00068 / prompt-token; $0.00160 / completion-token- Effective price: ~9% below your current blended rates- Migration credit: $85,000 applied 100% on first invoice; clawback schedule pro-rated over 6 months if monthly minima not met- Add-ons: 4h onboarding + 1 performance tuning pass included

Option C — 18-month Growth Escape (max savings)- Commit: $3.0M over 18 months (avg $166k/mo)- Unit pricing (indicative): $0.00060 / prompt-token; $0.00145 / completion-token- Effective price: ~15% improvement vs current blended- Migration credit: $150,000 (50% upfront, 50% after 90 days conditional on usage thresholds)- Add-ons: 8h professional services, SLA uplift to 99.9% inference availability, and marketplace credits available for cloud vendor exit

Common commercial terms:
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing; Net 45 default (flexible by procurement request).
- Credits: subject to simple clawback tied to monthly committed minimums.
- Contract signature: DocuSign link provided for term sheet acceptance.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm which option (A/B/C) procurement wants in the Nov 9 packet.
2) If B or C, we will issue a term sheet and DocuSign envelope for signature and schedule a 2-week technical onboarding window.
3) For private networking/VPC or stricter controls, loop in Marissa (CC'd) and we will produce a short implementation checklist.

We attached the commercial sheet and a short migration-credit terms doc (migration-credit-terms.docx). HubSpot record: HBSP-98342. DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/ABC123-Redwood-Brightline

Happy to hop on a 30-min call this week to walk procurement through the options.

Best,
